title: Multi-node Operations & Reliability
description: Study rendezvous and rank configuration, nccl diagnostics and hangs, durable distributed checkpoints, and elasticity and recovery semantics. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Rendezvous and rank configuration
lessons.description: Write a startup checklist covering world size, ranks, endpoints, and device assignment.
lessons.conceptOverview: Distributed startup needs consistent membership, rank identities, and communication endpoints. Configuration errors can resemble model failures. Validate connectivity and a minimal collective before running a full training job, and record the environment needed to reproduce the launch.
lessons.whyItMatters: Validate group membership and connectivity with a minimal distributed test.

lessons.title: NCCL diagnostics and hangs
lessons.description: Distinguish a slow collective from a rank that never entered it.
lessons.conceptOverview: GPU collectives can hang because of mismatched calls, device failures, or network problems. Collect logs and rank-local timelines, then reduce the workload to a minimal reproduction. Treat timeout changes as diagnostic controls rather than proof that the underlying issue is solved.
lessons.whyItMatters: Compare rank participation and logs before only increasing timeouts.

lessons.title: Durable distributed checkpoints
lessons.description: Design a commit marker or manifest policy that prevents partial checkpoints from appearing complete.
lessons.conceptOverview: A distributed checkpoint needs complete shard coverage and a consistent logical training step. Publish a checkpoint as usable only after its components are durably written and validated. Restore tests should include changed placement when that is a supported requirement.
lessons.whyItMatters: Validate complete checkpoint state before marking it ready to restore.

lessons.title: Elasticity and recovery semantics
lessons.description: List the settings that must be reconsidered when world size changes after a failure.
lessons.conceptOverview: Changing worker membership affects data assignment, effective batch size, and optimizer scheduling. Recovery must define what happens to partially completed work and random state. Elastic execution improves availability only when its statistical and operational semantics are understood.
lessons.whyItMatters: Define optimization and data-consumption behavior during membership changes.
